# Station history

## 1871, the founding

The station was built on Marrow Point in 1871 after the wreck of the schooner
Linnet. The first keeper was Odo Fenwick, who served for nineteen years.

## 1904, the new lens

A first-order Fresnel lens replaced the oil lantern in 1904. The old lantern was
sold to a chandler in the next town and is now lost.

## 1938, the great storm

In October 1938 a storm broke the gallery rail and flooded the cellar. The
keepers saved the almanac and the ledger by carrying them up to the lamp room,
but the whole season's lamp oil was lost to the sea.

## 1962, the automation attempt

A plan to automate the light was drawn up in 1962 and dropped within a year,
because the harbour board refused to pay for the cable.

## 1987, the cooperative

The Marrowdale Lighthouse Cooperative was formed in 1987 to take over the
station from the harbour board. Members pay a yearly share and work two weeks
of keeping duty each summer.

## 2003, the restoration

The tower was repointed and the gallery rail rebuilt in 2003, using a grant
that Ines Calder applied for over three winters.
